elements.name: init
elements.brief: Starts the client. Call it as early as possible. Sentinel keeps the table it is
elements.description:
Starts the client. Call it as early as possible. Sentinel keeps the table it is
given, filling in defaults and its `tags` and `extra`; `set_tag` and `set_extra`
write into it.

elements.name: add_breadcrumb
elements.brief: Records something that happened, sent with every later event. Sentinel adds a
elements.description:
Records something that happened, sent with every later event. Sentinel adds a
`timestamp` to the table and keeps the last 10. Does nothing before `init`.

elements.name: set_tag
elements.brief: Sets a tag sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.
elements.description: Sets a tag sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.

elements.name: set_extra
elements.brief: Sets extra data sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.
elements.description: Sets extra data sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.

elements.name: capture_exception
elements.brief: Sends an error to Sentry. With `config.set_error_handler` on, every uncaught error
elements.description:
Sends an error to Sentry. With `config.set_error_handler` on, every uncaught error
is already sent through this. Raises before `init`. At most 10 events are sent per
300 seconds; a throttled event goes to `callback` as an error.

elements.name: capture_message
elements.brief: Sends a message to Sentry. Raises before `init`. At most 10 events are sent per
elements.description:
Sends a message to Sentry. Raises before `init`. At most 10 events are sent per
300 seconds; a throttled event goes to `callback` as an error.

properties.name: dsn
properties.brief: Where events are sent. `init` asserts it is a string that parses as
properties.description:
Where events are sent. `init` asserts it is a string that parses as
`{PROTOCOL}://{PUBLIC_KEY}@{HOST}/{PATH}{PROJECT_ID}`.

properties.name: debug
properties.brief: Print what Sentinel sends. Defaults to `false`.
properties.description: Print what Sentinel sends. Defaults to `false`.

properties.name: dry_run
properties.brief: Build events without sending them; each callback receives the id `"(dry run)"`. Defaults to `false`.
properties.description: Build events without sending them; each callback receives the id `"(dry run)"`. Defaults to `false`.

properties.name: gameanalytics
properties.brief: Also report each captured exception to GameAnalytics when that extension is
properties.description:
Also report each captured exception to GameAnalytics when that extension is
present. Every exception then needs a `traceback`, or `capture_exception` raises.
Defaults to `false`.

properties.name: send_timeout
properties.brief: HTTP request timeout in seconds. Defaults to `30`.
properties.description: HTTP request timeout in seconds. Defaults to `30`.

properties.name: set_error_handler
properties.brief: Install a Lua error handler that captures every uncaught error. It takes the
properties.description:
Install a Lua error handler that captures every uncaught error. It takes the
single `sys.set_error_handler` slot, replacing any handler set before `init`.
Defaults to `true`.

properties.name: load_previous_crash
properties.brief: Submit the crash dump a previous session left, from inside `init`. Defaults to `true`.
properties.description: Submit the crash dump a previous session left, from inside `init`. Defaults to `true`.

properties.description: The release id sent with every event.

properties.description: The distribution, to tell builds or deployment variants of one release apart.

properties.brief: Called after an uncaught error is captured; only installed with
properties.description:
Called after an uncaught error is captured; only installed with
`set_error_handler`. The first return value is concatenated into a log line, so
returning nothing raises inside the error handler.

properties.description:
Called from `init` after a previous session's crash dump is captured. The first
return value is concatenated into a log line, so returning nothing raises out of
`init`.
